subject: Urgent: Proposed transient subprocessor for streaming-metrics — impact & rollback plan
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@streamlytics.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@streamlytics.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed transient subprocessor for streaming metrics ingestion

Hi Logan / Ben,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. As discussed, we have a short-term partner we'd like to route a subset of anonymized streaming-metrics to for feature experimentation: Nimbus Insights (contractor). They would only receive aggregated, pseudonymized metrics (no raw prompts or identifiable tenant IDs).

Key points in the attached one-pager:
- Scope: 6 weeks; metrics aggregation pipeline only (latency + error rates, no content)
- Data minimization: retention 7 days at Nimbus, then purged
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.3; at-rest encrypted with customer-managed keys at Nimbus (we can provide KMS ARN)
- Access: SSO + read-only analytics role; no service account access to logs

We know you require the full dataflow map and SOC-coverage proof. Attaching the proposal (streamlytics_subproc_proposal_v1.pdf) and a high-level diagram. Can your security/compliance team confirm whether this qualifies as a "temporary" subprocessor under our DPA? Also, any required addendum language we should include in their subprocessor agreement?

We appreciate a quick turnaround — the experiment is scheduled to begin 2026-12-06.

Best,
Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Data Partnerships | StreamLytics
attachments: streamlytics_subproc_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf), streaming_metrics_dataflow.png (png)

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@streamlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed transient subprocessor for streaming metrics ingestion

Hi Asha — thanks for the materials and the clear scope. Copying our internal leads so we can triage quickly.

Marissa / Mina: please see attachments from StreamLytics. High-level asks we need to close before approving:
1) A one-page dataflow that shows where pseudonymization occurs (currently looks like it happens in StreamLytics prior to egress — please confirm).
2) Evidence of the Nimbus security posture: SOC2 Type II report or equivalent; if unavailable, at minimum an internal security questionnaire + penetration test summary.
3) Clarify KMS ownership: StreamLytics said "customer-managed keys at Nimbus" — we need the KMS account owner and key policy language.
4) Rollback plan and guardrails: ability to stop forwarding instantly and proof of deletion after 7 days (audit APIs).

Ben: FYI this looks like a potential short-term expansion opportunity but we must ensure the DPA language covers the temporary processor flow.

Asha: If you can provide the SOC2 report and the updated diagram (with the pseudonymization step highlighted) by Tue 2026-12-01 EOD PST we can escalate to legal for an addendum review. Also attach any contractual language Nimbus wants to use.

I'll schedule a quick 30-min thread to resolve open items if necessary.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai; Asha Patel <asha@streamlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed transient subprocessor for streaming metrics ingestion

Quick commercial note from my side — thanks for looping me in. A couple items from procurement/sales: 
- If Nimbus needs to be added to our subprocessor roster, our standard procedure is to require a short onboarding questionnaire + a 1-month trial window with monitoring enabled. Could StreamLytics accept a clause requiring immediate suspension of forwarding upon discovery of any non-compliance?
- We should also capture the potential incremental egress/ingress costs. Asha — do you have an estimate of the additional bandwidth or storage that will traverse Nimbus during the 6-week test?

I don't want red tape to block the experiment but we need to make sure the approval path and stop-gap are in place. Happy to jump on the call Logan suggested.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; Asha Patel <asha@streamlytics.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed transient subprocessor for streaming metrics ingestion

Thanks all — reviewing now. Quick notes from Legal & Privacy: 
- Provisional approval conditionally granted pending evidence: (1) SOC2 Type II or completed third-party security questionnaire; (2) explicit KMS principal and key policy; (3) confirmation of pseudonymization step occurring on StreamLytics side prior to egress.
- DPA addendum: we'll prepare a short temp-subprocessor addendum (max 2 pages) that includes: purpose-limited processing, max retention (7 days), deletion confirmation API, immediate suspension clause, and audit rights.
- Please note we will not permit forwarding of any data that contains raw user content or tenant identifiers. If Nimbus cannot guarantee the KMS policy or deletion proof, we will require the data to be routed to our dedicated audit buffer (redwood-sec-audit) instead.

Asha — if you can grant access to the requested docs by Tue 2026-12-01 12:00 PST, Legal will aim to turn the addendum around within 24 hours. Also include the contact at Nimbus who will sign the addendum so we can route DocuSign directly.
